spec.explanation: The factor averages the daily close_position (where the close sits in the day's high-low range) over the trailing 20 days to capture persistent end-of-day order-flow imbalance, then cross-sectionally ranks it so the signal is comparable across stocks. High values indicate sustained closing-auction demand / informed accumulation not yet fully priced, predicting positive 5-day forward returns; low values indicate persistent selling into the close. The rank makes the factor dollar-neutral and robust to outliers, and the 20-day smoothing distinguishes persistent accumulation from one-day flow noise.

spec.explanation: The daily signal -sign(gap)*fade is positive when an overnight gap is absorbed against its direction (positive gap fading intraday, or negative gap bought back) and negative when the intraday move confirms the gap. Summing over 5 days captures persistent absorption, and rank() makes the score cross-sectionally comparable so we can go long the strongest absorption names and short the weakest, dollar neutral.

spec.explanation: range/ts_mean(range,20) measures range expansion versus its own 20-day baseline; volume/adv20 measures volume confirmation versus its ADV baseline. Each is cross-sectionally z-scored to make the two dimensionless ratios comparable, and their difference is high when range expanded without volume support (noise-driven, mean-reverting) and low when range expansion was volume-confirmed (informed). Averaging this signal over 5 days smooths daily noise, and the outer rank() makes it cross-sectionally comparable; the leading negative sign shorts high noisome range-expansion names and longs volume-confirmed ones, consistent with the negative expected sign over the 5-day horizon.

spec.explanation: The factor takes the 20-day simple moving average of dollar volume (amount) per ticker, a point-in-time liquidity proxy, then cross-sectionally ranks it so units are comparable across stocks. Negating the rank makes the signal long low-amount (illiquid) stocks and short high-amount (liquid) stocks, capturing the illiquidity premium while being dollar neutral. Using amount rather than cap isolates trading liquidity from pure size, and the 20-day smoothing reduces noise and turnover for the 5-day holding horizon.

spec.explanation: The factor sums the trailing 20-day intraday_return per stock (point-in-time, using only data up to day t), then cross-sectionally ranks it so the signal is comparable across stocks. High cumulative intraday return captures sustained continuous-session accumulation by informed traders while stripping out overnight jump noise, so long high-rank and short low-rank names should exhibit momentum continuation over the 5-day hold. rank() is applied rather than zscore() since the raw summed-return units are already comparable but ranking improves robustness to outliers.
